::: {#fig-lagrange-line}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: lagrange-line-r
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot over the plane of concentric circles centered at the origin, in
#|   grey, with radii 0.5, 1 and 1.5, and a blue straight line 3 x1 plus 4 x2
#|   equals 5 running from upper left to lower right. The line touches the
#|   circle of radius 1 at the point (0.6, 0.8), marked by a vermilion circle,
#|   and stays outside the circle everywhere else. A vermilion arrow from the
#|   origin to that point is perpendicular to the line.
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 5
ll_theta_ll <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 201)
ll_circles_ll <- expand.grid(theta = ll_theta_ll, radius = c(0.5, 1, 1.5))
ll_circles_ll$x1 <- ll_circles_ll$radius * cos(ll_circles_ll$theta)
ll_circles_ll$x2 <- ll_circles_ll$radius * sin(ll_circles_ll$theta)
ll_line_ll <- tibble::tibble(x1 = c(-0.5, 2), x2 = (5 - 3 * c(-0.5, 2)) / 4)
ll_point_ll <- tibble::tibble(x1 = 0.6, x2 = 0.8)
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_path(
    data = ll_circles_ll,
    ggplot2::aes(x1, x2, group = radius), colour = "grey60"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = ll_line_ll, ggplot2::aes(x1, x2), colour = "#0072B2"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    ggplot2::aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = 0.6, yend = 0.8),
    colour = "#D55E00",
    arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.15, "inches"))
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = ll_point_ll, ggplot2::aes(x1, x2), colour = "#D55E00", size = 3
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.6, 2), ylim = c(-1.6, 2)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x1", y = "x2")
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: lagrange-line-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot over the plane of concentric circles centered at the origin, in
#|   grey, with radii 0.5, 1 and 1.5, and a blue straight line 3 x1 plus 4 x2
#|   equals 5 running from upper left to lower right. The line touches the
#|   circle of radius 1 at the point (0.6, 0.8), marked by a vermilion circle,
#|   and stays outside the circle everywhere else. A vermilion arrow from the
#|   origin to that point is perpendicular to the line.
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 5
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

ll_theta_ll = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 201)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4), layout="constrained")
for ll_radius_ll in (0.5, 1, 1.5):
    ax.plot(ll_radius_ll * np.cos(ll_theta_ll),
            ll_radius_ll * np.sin(ll_theta_ll), color="grey")
ll_x1_ll = np.array([-0.5, 2])
ax.plot(ll_x1_ll, (5 - 3 * ll_x1_ll) / 4, color="#0072B2")
ax.annotate("", xy=(0.6, 0.8), xytext=(0, 0),
            arrowprops={"arrowstyle": "->", "color": "#D55E00"})
ax.plot(0.6, 0.8, "o", color="#D55E00", markersize=8)
ax.set_xlim(-1.6, 2)
ax.set_ylim(-1.6, 2)
ax.set_aspect("equal")
ax.set_xlabel("x1")
ax.set_ylabel("x2")
plt.show();
```

:::

The [level curves](vector-calculus.qmd#def-level-curve) $x_1^2 + x_2^2 = c$ of the [objective](#def-objective-function) (circles) and the constraint line $3 x_1 + 4 x_2 = 5$.
The line touches the circle $c = 1$ at the [minimizer](#def-minimizer-over-feasible-set) $\tp{(0.6, 0.8)}$ (@exm-qp-equality),
and the [gradient](vector-calculus.qmd#def-vector-derivative) there, the arrow, is perpendicular to the line.

:::
